jobs.title: Senior Environmental Specialist - BLUvera
jobs.description:
Summary

BLUvera, Mortenson’s vertically integrated manufacturing and fabrication affiliate, is currently seeking a Senior Environmental Specialist to develop and run the environmental compliance program for our mid-sized, fast-growing manufacturing and prefabrication business. This role will assess current compliance gaps, resolve issues, and develop standard processes and procedures for environmental permitting, waste management, inspections, and facility start-up and close-out as our operations grow and change.

Responsibilities

Develop, implement, and lead the environmental compliance program for a fast-growing manufacturing business
Conduct environmental compliance gap analyses across facilities and drive identified issues through to resolution
Establish standard processes and procedures to ensure proper environmental permitting, waste management, inspections, and issue resolution
Obtain, maintain, and ensure compliance with environmental permits, with a primary focus on waste, air, and wastewater
Manage hazardous and non-hazardous waste programs in compliance with RCRA requirements
Prepare and submit required regulatory reports, including SARA Title III / Tier II reporting
Conduct facility environmental inspections and support regulatory agency inspections
Lead environmental close-out activities as the business moves out of facilities, including permit closures, waste removal, and required documentation
Support environmental due diligence for property acquisitions and leases
Develop and lead environmental training programs
Maintain operational knowledge of environmental issues in manufacturing, and other applicable standards, regulations, laws, and procedures
Communicate with various third parties including regulatory representatives, environmental consultants, waste vendors, and landlords

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, geology, environmental management, environmental science, or related field of study
Minimum of six years of related experience
Demonstrated environmental compliance experience and expertise in a manufacturing environment
Strong working knowledge of RCRA requirements and compliance
Experience with SARA Title III / Tier II reporting
Experience with environmental permitting and inspections, particularly for waste, air, and wastewater
Proven ability to build and run an environmental program in a growing organization, including gap analysis, issue resolution, and developing standard processes and procedures
Deep understanding of Federal, State, Provincial and local laws, policies, and procedures
Strong organization and self-direction skills with the ability to collaborate in a team atmosphere
Ability to communicate with consultants and governmental agencies
Current driver’s license
Ability to travel up to 25%
Preferred: Experience with environmental due diligence for property acquisition and leasing

A Few Benefits Offered Include

(for Non-Craft & Non-Union Craft working 25+ hours / week)

Medical and prescription drug plans that includes no additional cost vision coverage
Dental plan
401k retirement plan with a generous Mortenson match
Paid time off, holidays, and other paid leaves
Employer paid Life, AD&D, and disability insurance
No-Cost mental health tool and concierge with extensive work-life resources
Tuition reimbursement
Adoption Assistance
Gym Membership Discount Program

The base pay range for this role is $98,800 - $133,300. (Actual range is higher for the following office locations: Denver, CO and Chicago, IL – 5%, Seattle, WA, and Portland, OR – 10%, Washington, D.C. – 12.5%).

Base pay is positioned within the range based on several factors including an individual’s knowledge, skills, and experience, with consideration given to internal equity. This position is eligible for Mortenson’s incentive plan.

#Onsite

Please Make Note

Visa sponsorship is not offered for this position.
Our postings are typically open a minimum of 5 days and an average of 44 days.

About Bluvera

BLUvera, a Mortenson affiliate, is the leading manufacturer creating solutions that are industrializing the construction industry. We provide innovative building solutions that deliver faster, safer, and more predictable experience for construction projects. Our products are fabricated with unprecedented precision, accuracy, and speed, providing customers with a fast, cost-effective, and safer building solution.

Let’s innovate together.

About Mortenson

As a top builder, developer, and EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction), our expertise spans markets like sports, renewable energy, data centers, healthcare, and more. We are builders at heart, working to ensure the built environment has a lasting positive impact.

Let’s Redefine Possible®

Equal Employment Opportunity

Your uniqueness brings new and creative perspectives to the team. Mortenson is committed to providing equal opportunities of employment (EOE) to all individuals, regardless of your race, religion, gender, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, marital status or any other legally protected category.

Other Items to Note

Mortenson reserves the right to hire any individual without legal or financial obligation on unwanted solicitations. No agency emails, calls, or solicitations are accepted without a valid agreement.
Must be currently legally authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status, 0-1, TN, CPT, OPT, etc.). We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

jobs.title: Program Manager I, Idaho Water Resources Research Institute
jobs.description:
Program Manager I, Idaho Water Resources Research Institute

University of Idaho

Appointment Information

Working Title:
Program Manager I, Idaho Water Resources Research Institute

Division/College:
CALS Col of Agri Life Sciences

Department:
UOFNI Water Energy Resource Institute

Location:
Coeur d'Alene

FTE:
1

Advertising Pay Range:
$75,004.80 annually or higher depending on experience

Is this position contingent on work and/or funding:
True

FLSA Status:
Exempt

Type of Appointment:
Full Fiscal Year

Position Overview

This position supports the planning and completion of educational, outreach or professional programs; working with program staff, students, the public and/or agencies, to plan and oversee program activities. May lead a distinct area for the program such as outreach, assessment or financial management. Duties may include:

Participate in the development and implementation of program deliverables, services and activities
Coordinate a team with an array of talents and responsibilities
Collect, compile and summarize program data for reports
Participate in developing program operating goals, objectives and protocols
Maintain program budgets, monitoring and reviewing transactions for compliance with program requirements
Active participation in the development and submission of program proposals
Lead collection and compilation of program assessment data­
May supervise the work of others or lead a team to accomplish assigned goals
Other duties as assigned

Required Experience

Two years of program coordination or program management experience
Working in a team environment to accomplish shared goals
Collecting, compiling, summarizing and analyzing data for administrative reports

Required Education

Bachelor's Degree; four additional years of experience in program coordination (for a total of six years) may substitute for a Bachelor's Degree

Required Other

Valid driver's license and ability to meet requirements for driving university vehicles
Must be able to travel within Idaho and the surrounding region

Additional Preferred

Bachelor's or advanced degree in business administration, organizational leadership, management, project management, water resources, environmental or natural science, engineering, natural resource policy, or a closely related field
Formal project management training or certification (e.g., CAPM, PMP) and experience managing concurrent, interdisciplinary, inter-institutional, or transdisciplinary projects involving multiple investigators, funders, and deadlines
Experience contributing to organizational strategy, process improvement, or program administration
Experience coordinating advisory boards, governing boards, or standing committees, including agenda development and meeting materials
Experience administering sponsored program deliverables, reporting requirements, proposal submissions, or competitive proposal solicitation and review processes in a university or agency setting
Experience establishing working relationships with faculty, staff, administrators, and public, private, tribal, or governmental agencies; supervisory experience; and knowledge of water resource issues in Idaho and the surrounding region

Physical Requirements And Working Conditions

None

Posting Information

Open Until Filled:
True

Special Instructions to Applicants:
Applications received by December 3, 2026, will receive first consideration.

Please submit a CV/resume and a cover letter describing how your education, skills, and professional experience have prepared you for success in this role, as well as what excites you about this opportunity at the University of Idaho.

If you would like to receive a full position description, please email Heather at hbiersner@uidaho.edu and request that one be sent to you.

Visa Sponsorship:
Uncertain

Degree Requirement Timeline:
Degree required at time of hire

To apply, please visit: https://careers.uidaho.edu/jobs/program-manager-i-idaho-water-resources-research-institute-coeur-d-alene-idaho-united-states
